  • I try really hard not to judge a movie or TV show based on its source material and the changes made to it.
  • Alright, let’s get into the endings of these two projects that follow actor Jack Stapleton and his bodyguard, Hannah Brooks – who are played by CW icons Jared Padalecki and Leighton Meester, respectively, in the film – as they go from fake-dating to real love.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers for the movie Guarding Stars and the book The Bodyguard are ahead! You can stream the film with a Netflix subscription.

I try really hard not to judge a movie or TV show based on its source material and the changes made to it. In fact, I usually love it when a book-to-screen adaptation makes bold updates and takes creative liberties. However, when I watched Netflix’s Guarding Stars, which is based on Katherine Center’s novel, The Bodyguard, I couldn’t help but be baffled by a massive change that was made to the ending.

Alright, let’s get into the endings of these two projects that follow actor Jack Stapleton and his bodyguard, Hannah Brooks – who are played by CW icons Jared Padalecki and Leighton Meester, respectively, in the film – as they go from fake-dating to real love.

In Center’s book, The Bodyguard, after all covers are blown and everyone thinks Jack is safe, he's taken hostage. When Hannah shows up for a date with him, Jack tells her to go away in an effort to keep her safe. Ultimately, she realizes Jack didn’t mean what he remarked, and that he was in danger. So, she ran back into his home to save him, and to make a long story short, after a fight and a gunshot wound for Hannah, they survived and lived happily ever after.

In the movie on the 2026 Christmas schedule, nearly the same thing happens, except one vital change is made: Jack goes to Hannah’s apartment in Fresh York to confess his love. When he gets there, she tells him she has company and does not share his feelings. Once he leaves, he realizes she was lying and goes back to save her. Ultimately, a similar kind of struggle plays out, and Hannah and Jack make it through safe and only slightly scathed, with Jack taking the gunshot wound instead of Hannah.

According to recent reports, on the whole, this movie is very different from its source material. While it keeps the essence intact, a lot of the key elements of the novel are totally changed. However, this final sequence where Jack/Hannah gets taken hostage stays fairly similar; the film just switches who shows up and decides to save whom and who gets shot. So, why change it in the first place?

In a recent development, in the book, I loved that Hannah highlighted up to Jack’s house and saved him. It really showed off both how good she is at her job and how much she genuinely cares for the actor she was protecting. I also appreciated how that scene addressed her doubt about their relationship and made her realize that Jack really does love her.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In the movie, because Jack is the one who demonstrates up for Hannah, we don’t fully get all of that. However, we do get to see him be a more active participant in this whole fiasco. While she still ultimately saves him in this substantial mess, it starts with him trying to protect her. To an extent, I get it, because Jack is more involved in the fight. However, what I loved about the book was that Hannah used this situation as the moment where she finally realized their shared feelings and got to kick butt in the process. I wish that's what had happened in the movie.

Industry observers note that so, ultimately, while most of the changes in Guarding Stars didn’t bother me at all, this one did a bit. I just can’t understand why they’d swap the genders and have Jack go to save Hannah and keep the rest of the squirmish pretty much the same. However, it’s still a project on the 2026 movie schedule that’s worth a watch, and maybe a debate if you’ve also read the book.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You Must Remember This is a podcast dedicated, as its host Karina Longworth states in every intro, to exploring the secret and/or forgotten histories of Hollywood’s first century. Longworth, who is an LA–based writer and film preservationist, usually tells her stories in themed seasons. Those include Erotic 90’s, spanning the introduction of the NC-17 rating to Eyes Wide Shut; Dead Blondes (Marilyn Monroe, Jean Harlow, Veronica Lake); and a whole series exploring the web of connections Charles Manson had to Hollywood. It’s addictive, exhaustively researched, and narrated in a way that is both soothing and trancelike.

Longworth is a native Angeleno who has been writing about film for years. She was a film editor and critic at the LA Weekly for three years until 2012; wrote books on Al Pacino and Meryl Streep; and then started You Must Remember This is 2014. She’s also part of a film-loving couple: her husband of 8 years is the Knives Out writer and director Rian Johnson.

It has been revealed that the latest season of the podcast is called The Bisexuals, spotlighting the stories of actors and actresses whose love lives were often much more diverse than anything sanctioned by a studio. One star that the season discusses is Libby Holman, a singer and socialite who married the tobacco heir Zachary Smith Reynolds in 1931. Not only did she have a fruitful sex life with Tallulah Bankhead and Montgomery Clift, but she was known for her signature scent called Jungle Gardenia.

Industry observers note that in honor of that bombastic perfume that wafted off of her, Longworth, 46, collaborated with Joey Rosin, who formulated a fragrance, Bisexual. Vanity Fair spoke to Longworth about moviegoing in Los Angeles versus Fresh York, what she smelled like as a teenager, being in grad school in your 40s, and her thoughts about Quentin Tarantino’s film programming.

The interview that follows has been condensed for length and clarity.

Vanity Fair: What was the first perfume you remember wearing?

Karina Longworth: Coco Mademoiselle was really a big deal for me when I was 18, 19. It was one of the first perfumes that I ever knew about. I started with The Body Shop’s Tea Rose oil. I didn’t really have any female adult influences because my mom died when I was 11, and so I had to sort of figure out that whole world.

According to recent reports, have you always wanted to make a perfume? Are you a perfume nerd?

So I never had an ambition to make a perfume, but over the past 10 years, I’ve become really into perfume. I used to rent an office space in the same building as an independent perfumer, Jacqueline Ella Steele, whose brand was called Goest— which doesn’t exist anymore—but she made a perfume called Silent Films. She was the first person I contacted about trying to formulate this perfume. But she’s out of business. So that’s when I started asking around and I got led to Joey Rosin.

The idea came from your research?

Sources indicate that I got the idea because, in reading and writing about Libby Holman, there are all these anecdotes of her walking into a room in a cloud of Jungle Gardenia, to the point where, people who were attracted to her were attracted to it, and people who didn’t like her found it so disgusting. I thought there was something really interesting about that, how the same scent could be either attractive or repellent, depending on how you felt about the person wearing it.

Industry observers note that what does a bisexual smell like? In this case jungles and gardenia.

Personalities, voices and clothes all depend on who’s doing it.

It has been revealed that there’s this really incredible anecdote in Patricia Bosworth’s Montgomery Clift biography about how one of Montgomery Clift’s friends was at a party at Treetops, Libby Holman’s estate, and she was looking for the bathroom, and accidentally walked into her bedroom, and the bed was a tangle of white satin sheets, and there’s a giant bottle of barbiturates on the nightstand and everything just reeked of Jungle Gardenia. She was grossed out, but then she also got the impression this is Libby and Monty’s sex lair.

Were you trying to recreate the smell?

According to recent reports, we didn’t try to copy the exact old fragrance. Joey does his research, and he did research into what the original notes were. But we talked about not wanting it to be a slavish copy, and instead just trying to evoke for both of us what jungle would smell like with gardenia, and how that could evoke Libby’s story. And so we played around with adding different types of smoke to it.

Have you ever been in a jungle?

It has been revealed that I’ve been to Tahiti. I’m trying to think if I’ve ever been to a jungle. We talked a lot about tropical plants and what the dirt would smell like, and the heat. It’s like hot weather almost has a smell. But then pairing that with this kind of old lady scent of gardenia. I went to visit his studio in Brooklyn a few times and he mailed some samples to me in Los Angeles. And by that point, it was like four iterations that were almost exactly the same. So it was just about what was giving me the best vibe.

You were living in LA for the process?

I was living alone in Rochester, N.Y. in a depressing situation because of the weather and being very alone, having no social life.

In a recent development, but you loved your grad school program, right? I forget the name but I know it’s long.

Recent findings suggest that L. Jeffrey Selznick School of Film Preservation at the George Eastman Museum. I got so much out of the program, but it was grueling, physically, and mentally, and emotionally. It was really difficult to suddenly be living alone in a place where I felt like I had no one I could really talk to.

So you were in an entirely new, but temporary situation.

I started relying on scented candles to improve my mood and to change my mood. If I got home feeling terrible, the fragrance was helpful. I also had nowhere to wear perfume. At first I thought I would just make a candle, and then as I started learning more about fragrance, I learned that candles have to go through a much more rigorous process. And it takes a lot longer. We were not going to be able to get it done in time to have a presale like we have during the podcast season. But in the future, I would like to do a signature scent for You Must Remember This and have it available as a perfume and a candle.

It would be classic, but in a different way. I’m very inspired by the signature scent that they have at the Chateau [Marmont].

Recent findings suggest that there has been a lot of talk about moviegoing being back. How has your tour been?

In a recent development, it has been great. In Savannah they sold 400 tickets to a very obscure, pre-code movie on a Friday night.

Sources indicate that people must ask you a lot of podcast questions. What are your tips?

I say I don’t know what form yours is going to take, but mine takes the form of writing an extremely detailed script, and then sitting by myself in a room and reading it into a microphone.

I built a recording studio. I bought a little house in Laurel Canyon at the end of a private road, like at the end of a cul-de-sac, but you feel like you’re in the middle of the forest. I bought it from this woman who had lived there for 15 years and was kind of an all-purpose healer. She basically built a soundproof room with clay on the walls and crystals embedded into the clay, where she would do sound baths with them. When I saw this house, it was just perfect.

Which city has a better movie scene, Fresh York or LA?

New York’s way better than LA, but LA is getting better.

According to recent reports, did someone buy the Vista? I loved that theater.

It has been revealed that [Quentin] Tarantino owns the Vista. Because it’s Tarantino, he won’t let them show anything digital. It has to be a film print, and so he’ll show a new movie if there’s a print, like The Odyssey played there, Sinners played there. But when there isn’t a new movie out that is on a print, he programs whatever he wants to see. He also does a lot of like Saturday morning matinees of classical Hollywood cinema that is just his taste, you know. Sometimes it’s my taste, sometimes it’s not. It’s a lot of Jerry Lewis. But one thing I will say for Tarantino is that when he discovers a filmmaker or genre or something from the past, he highlights. He’s been showing all these William Beaudine silent films, and I think that’s great because silent film has really fallen out of fashion in LA.

I was leaving to interview you today and someone noted, “Oh, I love that podcast,” and was talking about the Manson series. Is that your most popular?

According to recent reports, it changes. Increasingly, people are asking about the Polly Platt series.

Do you know what the next series is going to be?

Sources indicate that I have two ideas that would involve talking to people or family members of subjects who have passed away, but who could give me access to sort of the family lore. I am in contact with both of those families, but I need to kind of do the legwork, talking to them more and figure out which story makes the most sense. I also sketched out a very long season about the three stars of Rebel Without a Cause. That is something that people have been asking me to do for years. But the thing that stops me from doing it is that we still don’t know exactly what happened to Natalie Wood. But that’s kind of in my back pocket.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto games have never shied away from satirizing life, and GTA 6 has plenty of digs at famous brands, trends, and people. Not even gaming is immune to GTA's patented satire, especially if you're playing on Xbox, because there's no escape from PlayStation — or its legally distinct cousin, the JoySystem. Early in GTA 6, you'll get to bond with Jason's best pal, Cal. After maximizing the energy of Jason's bachelor pad with a little feng shui redecorating, the duo settles in for a night of booze, drugs, and video games on Booby's JoyStation console, which looks very similar to a PS5. It looks like this is the only gaming hardware in Leonida, since there are no Xbox Egg-Cube Stations X to play games on. The JoySystem isn't just for decoration either; after you've hung out with Bobby, you can return and play games on it. You can choose between an avant-garde experience or more immediate gratification with a pair of shooter games, and it's impressive how good these three games are on their own. From top-down action to stunning mystery that pokes fun at auteur-driven games, they're worth checking out. The JoySystem interface is also a 1:1 copy of the PS5 user interface, with the exact same layout for games and other apps — but given how much Sony is making from GTA 6 sales, we're guessing the company sees it as a cheeky little homage. But the controllers for the console? They look terrible: Eww. In real life, PS5 sales have absolutely dominated GTA 6 preorders and sales. Video game research company Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 sales have reached 24.58 million total units via pre-purchases and copies sold at launch, which works out to about $2.36 billion in gross revenue. Of that number, 18.44 million units are said to be PS5 copies of the game, of which Sony will get a 30% cut of sales. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

#4756. Tech Report: 10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1039 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1039 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has a pretty good track record on privacy.
  • Industry observers note that enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device.
  • Sources indicate that another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has a pretty good track record on privacy. The company bakes a number of protections into its OSes to keep your data from being shared or stolen. That remarked, you can make your Apple devices even more secure. There are plenty of opt-in settings that make it even harder for anyone to snoop on your device and activity. These are the best privacy hacks for your Mac.

Industry observers note that enabling the macOS Firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device. Turning on Stealth Mode prevents your Mac from even responding to these requests, essentially making it invisible to anything that's scanning a network you're connected to. This makes it more difficult for hackers and malware to know your device exists, much less attack it. This can interfere with certain essential activity when you're on your home network, but it's a valuable security setting when on public wifi. You can leave Firewall on all the time and enable Stealth Mode only as needed. Go to Settings > Network > Firewall, flip the toggle, then hit Options to manage Stealth Mode.

Sources indicate that another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating MAC addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi. If you use either your real MAC address or a fixed one (random but unchanging), it's easier to track your activity on that network, including when you arrive, how long you stay, and when you leave. Rotating addresses are best for public, shared networks you temporarily connect to, and don't require a login via a captive portal (like hotel wifi). You can turn this on for specific networks via Settings > Wi-Fi > [Network Name] > Details and change Private Wi-Fi address to Rotating.

Images and screenshots contain metadata, such as timestamps, device and hardware details, and, in the case of photos, physical location. Much of this information is stripped automatically when you share files to social media or via encrypted messaging apps, but if you're sending them via text or email, posting to forums, or sharing over AirDrop, metadata remains intact. You can easily remove metadata from your images right on your desktop. Select the file and hit control + click to bring up an options menu, then go to Quick Actions > Convert Image. Uncheck the box next to Preserve Metadata, then hit Convert. (This is also useful for quickly converting HEIC to JPEG without opening a separate app.).

Apple collects information about your device for diagnostic purposes or to improve apps and services, some of which is shared with third-party app developers. This may include crash and usage data as well as recordings and transcripts of Siri interactions and iCloud analytics. You can disable sharing for some or all of these categories under Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

You may be surprised by the number of apps and system services that use your device's location in the background. You should definitely disable location services for third-party apps that don't require location to function. You can find these toggles under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services. You can also turn off location permissions for some Apple apps and services if you're not using them on your device, like Weather and Maps. Finally, tap System Services and disable location for any non-essential features—at the very least, disable "Mac Analytics" and "Significant Locations & routes" (which lets your Mac and other iCloud devices learn locations and routes you use often).

Third-party apps on your Mac that need access to your device's camera and microphone have to request permission, and it's easy to grant this in the moment and then forget that you've allowed it. You should regularly audit which apps have these permissions and revoke access from those that don't need them on a day-to-day basis. Disabling them forces the app to ask again. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone or Camera to see the allowed apps and flip the toggle to disable permissions.

Another permission type you may have granted without much thought is local network access. This allows third-party apps to discover and communicate with other devices—printers, smart speakers, and IoT devices—on your home wifi. While this may be useful for services like Spotify that cast to connected hardware, other utilities, media apps, and games probably don't need to be mapping your network in the background. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network to audit permissions and disable those that aren't needed.

Another important permission to check concerns third-party apps that have access to your Mac's full disk, which includes data from Mail, Messages, Safari, Home, Time Machine, and admin settings. If an app only works with files you explicitly open and save, it doesn't need full disk access. Legitimate use cases may include antivirus and malware scanners, productivity tools, or backup utilities that you trust. You can also audit which apps have access to specific files and folders. This is under Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access or Files & Folders.

If you're using iCloud to store photos, files, and device backups, your data is encrypted on Apple's servers and in transit. Apple still holds the decryption key, which is useful if you somehow get locked out of your account and need help recovering it, but for sensitive data—including device backups—end-to-end encryption is the most secure way to ensure no one but you can gain access. Advanced Data Protection is an opt-in setting for iCloud that encrypts your information end to end. You'll need to set up an alternative recovery method, such as your device passcode with two-factor authentication, a recovery contact, or a recovery key. Be careful, though: If you lose access to this recovery method, you will lose your data. You can enable Advanced Data Protection on your Mac under System Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Advanced Data Protection > Turn On. Note that some iCloud data, including passwords and payment methods, are already end-to-end encrypted by default.

According to recent reports, apple TV today celebrated two Grammy nominations, one of which further establishes a canceled show as an unlikely awards success story. Here are the details.

Earlier this year, the Broadway adaptation of Apple TV’s ‘Schmigadoon!’ won four Tony Awards, including Best Musical, making Apple TV an EGOT winner by completing its collection of Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony awards.

‘Schmigadoon!’ premiered on Apple TV in 2021 and ran for two seasons, ending in 2023. In January 2024, show creator Cinco Paul confirmed that, although the third season had already been written with 25 newly introduced songs, Apple decided not to move forward with it.

Even before the Broadway adaptation’s Tony wins in June, a May report had raised hopes for the show’s return, revisiting an earlier interview in which ‘Schmigadoon!’ creator Cinco Paul revealed that there had been discussions about reviving it.

While there have been no further updates on a potential revival since then, fans got another reason to celebrate today, as the Broadway cast recording of ‘Schmigadoon!’ has been nominated for Best Musical Theater Album at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

It will compete against CHESS the Musical, The Lost Boys, Ragtime, and Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York).

Additionally, ‘Widow’s Bay‘ earned a nomination for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media, putting composer David Fleming up against the soundtracks of ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘One Battle After Another,’ ‘Project Hail Mary,’ and ‘Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu‘.

The 2027 Grammy Awards will take place on Sunday, February 7, 2027. To check out the full list of nominees, follow this link.

Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month or as part of the Apple One bundle. It features hit TV demonstrates and movies like Ted Lasso, Severance, The Studio, The Morning Show, Shrinking, and Silo.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned.
  • Somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned.
  • CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent," a statement from Cyberleek reads (via Kotaku).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somehow, Cyberleek, the notorious hacker behind multiple Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, has returned. This time, the infamous leaker is threatening to release the executable file for a working build of the Xbox version of the game hosted on their site, provided the public helps raise their meme coin to a $15 million market cap. "It is done. CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent," a statement from Cyberleek reads (via Kotaku). "Now. Every file except one--the main executable--held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1YEHOKYVTho The files on Cyberleek's site reportedly clock in at over 200GB, which would line up with the Xbox version of the game, but there's no guarantee they're the actual GTA 6 data or a collection of malware waiting to be downloaded onto a PC. The hacker added that if their demands aren't met, they'll release the executable needed to play GTA 6. However, there's no guarantee the game can be emulated, and Cyberleek added that they'll "work to get a PS5 build" if people keep supporting them. This isn't the first time Cyberleek has threatened to release a pirated build of GTA 6; back in October, they promised to do so if their meme coin reached $30 million in value. While this didn't happen--and the coin eventually crashed out--they did drop several GTA 6 video clips throughout the month showing off more of the game in action. While Cyberleek initially claimed to act in gamers' interests when they first burst onto the scene, they true motives were swiftly revealed when they started hyping up their meme coin--reportedly part of a pump-and-dump scheme. While Cyberleek has yet to be identified, their actions did lead to GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games to glitch a statement, in which it described the leaks as "heartbreaking" after years of work on the game. Rockstar's parent firm, Take-Two, filed multiple subpoenas, asking Microsoft and Discord to help identify CyberLeek. So far, the hacker remains a mystery.

The Surprising History of the Royal Walkabout

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2224 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, “I have to be seen to be believed,” the late Queen Elizabeth II once noted.
  • In a recent development, but three controversial royals, the former Prince Andrew, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, almost certainly will not be there.
  • It has been revealed that for centuries, commoners were lucky to get a glimpse of royals riding a horse on a march across the country or nodding from a carriage on the way to the opening of parliament.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, “I have to be seen to be believed,” the late Queen Elizabeth II once noted. And on Christmas Day, the royal family will be seen en masse during their annual walkabout on their way to services at St. Mary Magdalene Church on the Sandringham estate. For years, the holiday stroll, which features major and minor royals mingling with the public, has been a milestone event on the royal calendar.

In a recent development, but three controversial royals, the former Prince Andrew, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, almost certainly will not be there. While Andrew has disappeared into his upcoming life at Marsh Farm in Norfolk, Harry and Meghan have continued the tradition of the walkabout, reportedly infuriating the palace with a planned meet-and-greet with a small group of well-wishers in Nottingham. Although no longer working members of the royal family, it seems the couple knows the value and the power of this famous tradition, whose origins are far more recent than many believe.

It has been revealed that for centuries, commoners were lucky to get a glimpse of royals riding a horse on a march across the country or nodding from a carriage on the way to the opening of parliament. The first Buckingham Palace balcony appearance was not until 1851, when Prince Albert came upon the idea of Queen Victoria appearing to celebrate the Great Exhibition of London.

The leading figure behind the idea of making the monarchy more visible to the public was a surprising one: the dour, but savvy George V, who ascended the throne in 1910. “I may be uninspiring,” he admitted, “but I’m damned if I’m an alien.”.

Industry observers note that queen Elizabeth II and Prince William waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace during Trooping the Colour on June 16, 1990. Pictured: Prince Edward, Duchess Of York, Queen Mother, Princess Margaret, Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Philip, Prince William, The Grand Duchess Josephine Charlotte Of Luxembourg, Prince Harry, Prince Charles, Lord Frederick Windsor, Princess Diana and Lady Rose Windsor.

These royal appearances ramped up significantly during the first World War, when the royal family came under scrutiny for their German lineage. George visited everyday soldiers on the Front, and Queen Mary and her children spent hours visiting the wounded in hospitals.

“George took ‘getting out and about’ to upcoming levels. He visited industrial areas and poor housing, went down a coal mine and went on a relentless round of opening hospitals and inspecting regiments,” royal news website Royal Central notes. “Queen Mary once retorted to a princess complaining about yet another hospital visit: ‘We are the royal family—and we love hospitals.’”.

Recent findings suggest that however, these events were still carefully curated, with a distance maintained between the royal family and those they were visiting. It was not until 1939, that the first unofficial walkabout occurred, when King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (better known as the Queen Mother) went to tour Canada on a goodwill tour in the midst of the looming war. In May, the couple laid a wreath at Ottawa National War Memorial while an estimated 10,000 veterans looked on.

Sources indicate that overcome with emotion, the royal couple decided to go into the crowd to speak with onlookers. A CBC radio journalist watching the scene could hardly have sounded more in awe. “They all look most happy, most excited,” the reporter stated. “One had the hand of the queen in one hand and the hand of the king in another. A delighted expression.”.

George and Elizabeth were equally touched, and continued these meet-and-greets throughout the tour. “I lost my heart to Canada and to Canadians, and my feelings have not changed with the passage of time,” the Queen Mother recalled.

In a recent development, known for her effusive personality and warmth, the Queen Mother became a pro at speaking with everyday subjects. During World War II, George and Elizabeth were praised for going among the people in bombed out areas devastated by the Blitz, listening to their woes and offering encouragement and strength.

Queen Elizabeth II on walkabout in Launceston, Tasmania, during her tour of Australia, 1970.

It has been revealed that but it was not until Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip toured Australia and Newly introduced Zealand in 1970 that the modern walkabout was truly introduced into the British royal calendar. There are different origin stories about how the modern walkabout came to be. One version asserts that it was a spontaneous decision of the Queen to walk to her next stop in order to chat, shake hands and accept flowers from schoolchildren in New Zealand.

Others say that first walk was the brainchild of the modernizing Australian courtier William Heseltine, known as the “mastermind behind the monarchy.” A firm believer in making the family seem more approachable and normal, he was also behind the 1969 Royal Family documentary. But if that project proved to be controversial, the walkabout (a term coined as a result of the tour) was a smash hit.

According to Kitty Kelley, the first royal walkabout did not occur in London until 1972, during the celebration of Elizabeth and Philip’s 25th wedding anniversary. “People were agog; their sovereign had never been known to speak to ordinary people,” Kelley writes in The Royals. “This was the first royal walkabout London had ever seen, and flag-waving Britons cheered as the Queen, the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Charles, and Princess Anne melted into the crowd, greeting people and trying to make the royal family appear less remote.”.

While the Queen reportedly enjoyed the intimacy of the walkabout, not every royal family member was quite as thrilled. “At nineteen years old suddenly being dropped in the middle of the street, suddenly being told to pick someone and talk to them,” Princess Anne said. “Fun? No, I don’t think so. A challenge.”.

Queen Elizabeth II visits the Town Hall in Sydney with Emmet McDermott, Lord Mayor of Sydney, during her tour of Australia, May 1970.

Recent findings suggest that soon, the walkabout was a major part of every royal’s schedule, and family members had to learn how to do them—like it or not. “I learnt the way a monkey learns—by watching its parents,” King Charles once stated.

Recent findings suggest that during international tours, the walkabouts made a packed schedule even more tiring, but Queen Elizabeth II never faltered. “On a tour of Canada, visiting Saskatchewan, the Canadian minister Alvin Hamilton was concerned that the Queen had been on her feet all day and had not even requested a ‘health break,’” Karen Dolby writes in The Wicked Wit of Queen Elizabeth II. “Her private secretary breezily replied that the Minister for Northern Affairs and National Resources need not worry, ‘Her Majesty is trained for eight hours.’ It’s impossible not to wonder about the training sessions.”.

It has been revealed that she also leaned upon her sense of humor when meeting folks of all different stripes. “On a walkabout in Scotland, a helpful observer commented that she looked just like the Queen, to which she swiftly replied, ‘How reassuring,’” Dolby notes.

In a recent development, according to Dolby, the Queen also developed a system to communicate with her staff while talking with the public. If things were going well, she held her handbag in the crook of her left arm. If she wanted someone to relieve her so she could move on, the handbag was dropped to her side.

But the person who truly transformed the modern walkabout was Princess Diana, much to her husband Prince Charles’s chagrin. “Charles was smart enough to see what a stunning political asset Diana had become—but he was also deeply disturbed by all the adoration coming his young wife’s way,” Tina Brown writes in The Diana Chronicles.

From the start it was clear the young Princess had a connection with everyday people unlike any other royal. During a walkabout while touring Wales in 1981, Charles joked, “I seem to do nothing but collect flowers these days, I know my role.”.

In a recent development, as Dianamania swept the world, the Princess became more and more comfortable with connecting with her often-rabid fans. Far from a stiff gloved handshake, she would clasp hands gloveless, hug well-wishers, kneel to speak with children. Frustrated that Diana constantly pulled focus, Charles delivered pithy one-liners with a forced smile. At one walkabout, the crowd openly groaned when they realized Charles was coming to their side, not Diana. “It’s not fair is it?” Charles quipped to the crowd. “You’d better ask for your money back.”.

According to recent reports, but despite Charles’s jealousy, he could not deny the impact Diana had during these walkabouts. “Everyone was really buoyed up to see her and she was making an effort to go along and speak to people and people appreciated the effort she put into meeting them,” one person she spoke with remembered. “I know it was her job but she gave that little bit extra to people that made her different and stand out.”.

Recent findings suggest that “She made people happy,” he noted. “It’s a rare gift.”.

According to recent reports, catherine, Princess of Wales, has followed in her mother-in-law’s footsteps as a walkabout all-star. According to historian Robert Jobson, Catherine was initially scared during the walkabout, offering up the stiff refrain, “Thank you so much. We are so delighted to be here,” over and over. But she promptly acclimated and has become known for her chatty and warm ways. “There’s a real art to walkabouts,” she has said. “Everybody teases me in the family that I spend far too long chatting. I still have to learn a little bit more, and to pick up a few more tips, I suppose.”.

In fact, it has become a sport for the press to catch Prince William subtly attempting to move Catherine along, often eventually giving up. During the Christmas Day walkabout in 2024, she was the last royal to leave the receiving line, quipping “I think I’ve lost my family!”.

According to royal author Robert Hardman, King Charles can also be unusually chatty. No one quite wants to go up and go, ‘Sir, can you get a move on?’ he claims. “Instead, Queen Camilla will nudge him in the small of his back with the corner of her handbag.”.

But the predilection is one Camilla shares as well. On a walkabout in Wrexham, an irritated Charles was overheard telling an aide “Can we try to get [Camilla] back again? Please? We need to go! I was trying to wait for her, but she goes on!”.

Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend University of the South Pacific on October 24, 2018 in Suva, Fiji.

Learning the art of the walkabout—what to say, what not to say—is a lesson every royal must figure out, often on the job. When Meghan Markle married Prince Harry in 2018, she admitted her ignorance. “I never saw pictures or videos of a walkabout,” she claimed.

And with the advent of cell phones, the job has become much more difficult. “I’m glad that I’m not starting now because at least you had people to talk to. Now you don’t really. Phones are bad enough, but the iPads—you can’t even see their heads,” Princess Anne said.

And these engagements can occasionally go south. In 2018, the Duchess of Sussex was rushed out of a market in Fiji after the walkabout got out of hand. There are also the occasional overzealous fans, including recently when a woman attempted to kiss Prince William on the cheek. And who can forget the supremely uncomfortable walkabout at Windsor after the Queen’s death in 2022, when a warring William, Catherine, Harry and Meghan greeted public mourners. It was, Catherine reportedly stated, “one of the hardest things she’d ever had to do.”.

Recent findings suggest that walkabouts are also a logistical headache for royal protection officers. “You are always aware of who is in the crowd,” former royal bodyguard Simon Morgan explained to Hello! “That is one of the positives of our royal family, they always want to go and meet people and as a protection officer, you have to accept what their wishes are. The current trend of hugs, high fives and selfies, that’s going to continue, so the protection officer’s job is really brought to the front then, because the protection officer is constantly looking for what could go wrong, you are constantly working things through your mind for the ‘what if, what if, what if.’.

But the walkabout highlights no sign of disappearing anytime soon. And come Christmas Day, there will be cheers, hugs, and an enormous amount of quick, polite chats about the weather that citizens who wait and brave the winter cold will never forget.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that mark Harmon spoke on its origins in an interview with Cheat Sheet, and how a bit of improvisation became an iconic recurring bit.
  • In a recent development, michael is a hugely talented actor, as is every member of this cast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for years, Leroy Jethro Gibbs was the face of NCIS. His litany of rules and quirks was the heart and soul of the series, with his trademark head slap being one of them. As he's back in primetime on the Origins spinoff, I'm learning the slap all started with his former co-star, Michael Weatherly.

Industry observers note that mark Harmon spoke on its origins in an interview with Cheat Sheet, and how a bit of improvisation became an iconic recurring bit. Harmon set the scene far back before the 2026 TV schedule, all the way back to the first year of the series:.

In a recent development, michael is a hugely talented actor, as is every member of this cast. My memory of when that happened, we were doing a scene. And he was on a Navy ship and he was talking to a female petty officer. I think this was in year one, early. And he was doing what he does, which is sometimes stay on script and sometimes not. I just reached over and smacked him. I tried to put him back on line. It was an instinct. It wasn’t thought, I didn’t think about it, I just did it.

Funny to think this all started partly because Mark Harmon was frustrated with Michael Weatherly going off script. I could imagine filming days were long enough without improvisation that it could sabotage a scene that was perfectly written as-is. I can empathize with Harmon just wanting to move on, and giving Weatherly a smack on the head to remind him that other people would like to move on as well.

In fairness to Weatherly, Harmon's head slap could've caused a much bigger distraction had he completely broken character and gotten into a fight with his co-star. Fortunately, Harmon confirmed the Tony DiNozzo actor didn't miss a beat, and it became a part of the show's history:.

According to recent reports, to his credit, he stayed in the scene; he didn’t break. And I didn’t break. And the girl in the scene playing the petty officer, she was shocked, she was surprised. And she stayed there, and we just kept going. And people liked it. And every episode I was smacking him–maybe too much. We still do that occasionally, but sparingly. That’s where it came from.

It may not be the sole reason that NCIS is now a franchise generating billions of dollars across its lifetime, but it certainly contributed. Tony and Gibbs' relationship was one of the show's best parts in its early years, and many still remember it fondly.

What's funny about this story is that Michael Weatherly largely remembers it the same way, but added on detail that Harmon left out. In the moment, no one knew that the head smack was going to be something iconic in NCIS. It was only Season 1, and they were just a few episodes in.

Recent findings suggest that instead, Weatherly only remembers that he was goofing off, and everyone on set was mad at him afterward for potentially ruining a shot. It wasn't until they saw the head smack in the editing room that producers liked it and decided to make it a part of the episode and the show.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

These days, Weatherly's Tony doesn't get a ton of head smacks. He's right now the acting director of the NCIS team, and also occasionally jumping in to lend a hand in investigations. I don't imagine anyone wants to slap the boss man on the back of the head, but I'd be up for seeing someone try.

Recent findings suggest that NCIS continues on CBS on Tuesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. The entire evening is silly with spinoffs for the crime procedural, so anyone who isn't currently already aware of that should check it out!

The Prime Minister of the UK, Andy Burnham, has labeled Rockstar Games a "British success story" amid GTA 6's rave reviews and huge sales milestones. A spokesperson for his office told The Independent, "Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh, and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." Rockstar North is based in Edinburgh, Scotland, but GTA 6 was made by thousands of people across the globe. GTA is also historically linked to the UK, as the original game, 1997's Grand Theft Auto, was made by DMA Design in Edinburgh. Asked if the PM himself would play GTA 6, his office stated Burnham is too busy right now. "He won't be playing it," the spokesperson said. GTA 6 introduced on November 19 and reportedly sold nearly 25 million copies and earned $2 billion in revenue by launch day. The game boasts a mightily impressive 99 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic, meaning it's tied with the original Ocarina of Times for the highest aggregate review score for any game ever. GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, but many are expecting Rockstar to eventually announce an online mode for the game. According to reports, the upcoming version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could arrive in 2027, with a PC edition also coming that year.

The apples don’t fall far from the tree in Matthew McConaughey’s household.

The Oscar winner and wife Camila Alves’ three children looked all grown up and every bit at home as they made a rare red carpet appearance together on Thursday, November 19, at the Los Angeles premiere of Way of the Warrior Kid.

The couple’s eldest son, Levi McConaughey, was supported by his younger siblings, sister Vida, 16, and brother Livingston, 13, at the premiere of his latest movie, which costars Chris Pratt.

The sibling trio were all smiles as they posed for photos together. Levi looked suave in a dark suit with a light blue shirt, while Livingston opted for a light blue suit with a white T-shirt. Vida looked elegant in a white dress.

In a recent development, levi has been following in his famous dad’s acting footsteps in recent years. He first appeared alongside Matthew, 57, in The Lost Bus, which was released in 2025.

In a joint interview with his dad for People last year, Levi admitted he was beginning to feel the pressure of being Matthew McConaughey’s son.

“Yeah, it’s just starting,” Levi shared. “And as much as people can say, ‘Oh, you got this because of your father or your mother,’ they can open the door, but then it’s going to be up to me to do my thing once I get in there. That’s on me.”.

Levi said “you got to have some chops” to make it as an actor, adding, “And so, yes, it’d feel like it would be a disservice to them because of how hard they’ve worked to get to the position that they’re at to not take advantage of it, but also put in the work and get after it and do it.”.

In October 2025, Matthew remarked that his son earned his role in The Lost Bus on his own merit.

In a recent development, “I’m not putting that pressure on him either way. But he’s off to a great start, and he’s in the door,” Matthew noted on Sunday Today With Willie Geist.

Recent findings suggest that “As far as nepotism goes for me, Camila and I always say, ‘Don’t you ever feel entitled,’” he continued. “When he read for this role, I sent it to the casting director. She said, ‘I think it’s good enough to send to the director.’ And I went, ‘Pull his last name.’”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updates are generally good for your devices.
  • According to recent reports, sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel people are discovering this week.
  • Recent findings suggest that here's the situation: Following the November update, some customers are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updates are generally good for your devices. The latest Chrome revision, for example, patches an actively exploited security vulnerability, while Apple's latest updates stop people from seeing iMessages they shouldn't have access to. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

According to recent reports, sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel people are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November enhancement apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

Recent findings suggest that here's the situation: Following the November update, some customers are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the matter is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

To be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal issue. It's not like all Pixel customers are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

Luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some owners are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

According to recent reports, what does appear to work, however, is shutting your Pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

If your Pixel's camera is giving you grief following the November patch, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. As the concern does seem to be rather widespread, I wouldn't be surprised to see Google issue a patch in the coming days. But until then, turning your phone off for five minutes may be a decent compromise.

The Princess of Wales touched down in India this Monday for a whirlwind three-day visit to the country with her husband, Prince William.

The couple visited Mumbai for the sixth Earthshot Prize Summit, which took place on Tuesday. It marked the Waleses’ first joint overseas visit since Catherine’s cancer diagnosis.

Industry observers note that the busy schedule of engagements kicked off with a game of gully cricket—an informal version of the game played on the street. For the occasion, the Princess of Wales struck a balance between polished and casual, opting for crisp white Alexander McQueen trousers, paired with a white top layered under a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard.

The Princess of Wales debuted a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard for the outing.

The finishing touch? A matching set of green amethyst earrings and a drop necklace from one of Catherine’s favorite jewelry labels, Kiki McDonough. Catherine has at least 20 pairs of earrings from the jeweler, ranging from the blue topaz drops she wore to Royal Ascot to the green tourmaline, green amethyst and diamond earrings set in gold, designed specially for her to mark Princess Charlotte’s birth.

The apple green amethysts, which she wore in Mumbai, are among the lesser-seen designs in her collection but proved the perfect accessory for this first engagement.

While in Mumbai, the prince’s program focused on The Earthshot Prize and its mission to accelerate solutions to the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. The princess joined the prince for a number of engagements during the visit.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai on Monday.

During their time in Mumbai, the prince and princess also celebrated several of the deep cultural connections between the United Kingdom and India: cricket, fashion, and cinema.

Beginning with an engagement focused on the uniquely Indian passion of gully cricket andconcluding with a visit to the heart of Mumbai’s film industry, their royal highnessescelebrated the creativity, talent, and cultural influence that continue to shape modern India andstrengthen ties between the two countries.

The highlight of the visit was the Earthshot Prize ceremony on Tuesday, November 17. Five Earthshot leaders were given 1 million euros (about $1.1 million USD) to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions. Mumbai made perfect sense as the host city; India is home to more Earthshot Prize winners and finalists than any other country.

The Princess of Wales looked elegant in a lime green blazer layered over an all-white ensemble.

Recent findings suggest that since founding the prize in 2020, Prince William has attended all of the awards ceremonies: in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro. Catherine joined the prince in London in 2021 and again in Boston the following year, but has missed recent editions in the further corners of the globe. This was partly due to the princess’s restricted work schedule while she underwent treatment for cancer and spent time in recovery.

Industry observers note that it marked a return to the country for Prince William and Kate, who carried out a state visit in April 2016. The week-long tour saw the then Duke and Duchess of Cambridge explore Mumbai, Upcoming Delhi, Assam, and Bhutan, racking up a total of 22 engagements that saw them try their hand at cricket, meet Bollywood stars and royalty, and champion charitable causes close to their hearts.

It was one of four overseas trips taken by the couple that year. Although William and Kate still travel, it is with far less frequency as the couple prioritizes a stable family life. Their last major overseas tour was to the Caribbean in 2022.

Every Future Driving Game Needs to Steal This GTA 6 Feature

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (523 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I've written numerous times about my love for open-world driving games.
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has instantly joined my driving-game canon thanks to one tiny, but revolutionary, feature.
  • In a recent development, on the PlayStation 5 version of GTA 6, Rockstar Games has come up with a genius application for the DualSense controller's adaptive triggers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I've written numerous times about my love for open-world driving games. I love racing, but I also love cruising, taking in the landscape, setting out on road trips. My heart belongs to Test Drive Unlimited. I've written a tourist guide for the Forza Horizon series. One of my games of the year is the Road Trip DLC for American Truck Simulator.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has instantly joined my driving-game canon thanks to one tiny, but revolutionary, feature.

In a recent development, on the PlayStation 5 version of GTA 6, Rockstar Games has come up with a genius application for the DualSense controller's adaptive triggers. When driving, the right trigger (the throttle) provides gentle resistance when cruising at the speed limit. The effect is a sort of soft stop for the trigger; your finger rests easily there, but it's also easy to push past it when you want to put your foot down.

It has been revealed that I cannot overstate how much I love this. If you want to cruise, you no longer need to hover your finger in an approximate spot, making tiny adjustments to try to match speed with the traffic. You can just rest it against the soft stop, the way you just rest your foot on the accelerator pedal in a real car. It's so chill.

I don't always want to hurtle to my destination at full speed, even in a pure racing game like Forza. These beautiful open worlds are worth taking time to explore, seeing the sights and listening to the soothing drone of the engine. Sometimes tearing around everywhere at speed is noisy and stressful. In Forza Horizon, I adopt a more relaxed driving style by using manual gears and short-shifting to keep the revs low, but GTA 6's solution is way more elegant.

The pleasure of cruising in GTA 6 is only enhanced by the richness of the world Rockstar has created. It's not just gorgeous, it's teeming with life, incidents (I watched a plane crash into the swamp while rolling on the freeway), and overheard conversations. And there are the radio stations to enjoy, too. Cruising the humid streets of the Keys while pumping Kaleidoscope FM is such a vibe.

I also enjoy this feature when I don't want to cruise, because pushing past the soft stop on the trigger is so deliciously satisfying. The amount of resistance is perfectly calibrated. It gives you the feeling of slamming your foot down to engage kickdown in a car with an auto gearbox and feeling the car surge forward. It's dramatic and cool.

In a recent development, I want this cruising-speed soft stop in every open-world driving game. For now, that sadly only means driving games on PS5, because Xbox gamepads don't have adaptive triggers. But Forza Horizon 6 is coming to PS5 on Jan. 26. Playground Games, you have two months to add this feature to the PS5 version of your game. If you manage it, I vow to buy a second copy and return to the roads of Japan, cruising my way to road-trip heaven.
